content.title: About
content.content: Raw oysters are seafood harvested from mollusks of the family Ostreidae. They have a delicate briny flavor with a buttery finish, and their texture ranges from crisp to creamy depending on the variety. Oysters are typically served chilled, often with lemon wedges, mignonette sauce, or a splash of vinegar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oysters filter water, cleaning it of particles and bacteria; one gram of oysters can filter up to 50 liters of water per day.
They are a natural source of zinc, which supports the immune system.
In ancient cultures oysters were considered an aphrodisiac and used in fertility rituals.
There are over 100 edible oyster species, but commercial farming focuses mainly on three: Pearl, Kokos, and Pacific (Californian).
Oysters can change sex during their life, starting as males and later becoming females.

items.title: Rich in zinc
items.content: Zinc plays a role in immune function, wound healing, and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system health.

items.title: Low‑calorie high‑quality protein
items.content: Oysters provide complete protein that helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Rich in iron and selenium
items.content: These minerals are important for oxygen transport and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw oysters may harbor Vibrio vulnificus and other pathogens; people with weakened immune systems should avoid them.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Oysters naturally contain salt; those limiting sodium should monitor portion size.

items.title: Potential heavy metal accumulation
items.content: In certain regions oysters can accumulate cadmium or lead; choose products from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve raw oysters on a bed of ice, often with lemon wedges, mignonette, vinegar, or soy sauce. Open them with an oyster knife, then eat directly from the shell. They can also be lightly grilled or steamed if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep live oysters in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C, covering them with a damp cloth and placing them in a container that allows airflow. Do not wash them before storage. Use within 1‑2 days. Discard any oysters that remain open after a gentle tap.
